Use the attached original sprite sheets as exact style/camera references, but create genuinely NEW alternative architecture with different roof shapes, structural panel layouts and equipment arrangement, never a recolor. Native PNG RGBA, transparent_background=true, completely transparent empty background and gutters. 1536x1024 landscape, exactly a 4 columns by 4 rows layout, 16 isolated sprites row-major. Each cell is 384x256: the ENTIRE object, base, antenna, chimneys and lamps must fit within its own cell with at least 24px empty transparent margin on each side, never crop or overlap neighbors. Identical high-angle orthographic 2.5D camera as references, front facades face the lower image edge, zero perspective vanishing point, subdued earth/rust/dirty-concrete palette, fine tactile painted realism. No people, labels, lettering, cell borders, backgrounds, shadows outside the object's own base, magic, sci-fi, glow, shooting barrels, live water/charge indicators or flashing effects. Each is an alternative to the SAME building state/function and comparable footprint, never more floors or an upgrade. Low buildings have ONE real floor unless explicitly stated TWO. Preserve functional visual recognizability. Supply one and only one sprite per cell in the precise following order:
ROW 1: 1) expeditionOffice: one-floor expedition office with covered map counter without text, cargo cases, realistic radio antenna and revised pitched roof; 2) expeditionGarage: one-floor expedition garage with one wide steel roller door, roof ventilation, tyre racks and cases, no vehicles; 3) fireCistern: realistic vertical cylindrical firefighting water tank on small rectangular concrete base, pipework/hose reel, a CLEAR EMPTY vertical gauge housing on its RIGHT front side for a game-drawn water level; 4) dayGreenhouse: one-floor daylight greenhouse, CLEAR glass bays with crops and alternate pitched roof section layout.
ROW 2: 5) solarCourt: smaller ground solar courtyard with two rows of realistic photovoltaic panels, alternate supports and conduit arrangement, no extra capacity indicated; 6) radioRelay: low one-floor utility cabin with a tall visible steel antenna mast and radio aerials fitted entirely inside cell, new bracing/mast silhouette; 7) batteryCabinet: small pair of weathered metal backup battery cabinets with rearranged conduit and vent panels, no illuminated gauges; 8) batteryStation: one-floor backup battery shed with three cabinet bays and revised roof/cable layout, no live-charge indicators.
ROW 3: 9) batteryComplex: broad one-floor electrical reserve complex with large cabinet bank, separated switchgear and revised flat roof; 10) beacon: short emergency beacon on small concrete plinth, new caged cylindrical lamp hardware, lamp unlit; 11) streetlight: tall realistic simple single-head urban street lamp on small concrete base, distinct curved bracket and lamp housing, not switched on; 12) searchlight: ONE realistic directional searchlight on swivel mount and square concrete plinth, lamp head center clearly identifiable, no light beam or glow.
ROW 4: 13) perimeterLight: upright TWO-head perimeter light on realistic tripod/pole/concrete base with new bracing, heads unlit; 14) districtSearchlight: TWO large lamps side-by-side on a low heavy concrete swivel platform with cabinet, clear central pivot, no beam; 15) alarmTower: small open steel lookout tower with braced four legs, roofed lookout ONE elevated platform, realistic side stair and siren hardware, no person; 16) fireScreen: small freestanding fire-resistant corrugated metal panel reinforced with two concrete horizontal ribs on small feet, distinct stepped/riveted structural layout.
extendedRejectedGenerations.reason: 14 large components: garage/antenna and battery/streetlight touch.
